text: ACK org/README.md reorg. Phase 1 (plan file + adversarial review by pi GLM and qwen3.8-27b, then revision) is running in an Opus subagent now; no repo edits until you hear the reviewed plan summary from me. Will not commit without the owner's say-so. Also running here: GPU tuning subagent, v2/v3 benchmark overseers.

Best local 27B so far: Qwen3.8-27B Q2_K_L (bartowski GGUF, ollama q27-Q2_K_L) 59.4 gen tok/s at empty ctx, prompt 1,552 tok/s at 28.6k fill (peak prompt 1,622 tok/s at 8k fill, 32k baseline sweep); from the GPU-tuning probe running now, num_ctx 49152, KV q8_0, flash attention, 66/66 layers on the RTX 5080. Runner-up Q3_K_S 52.3 gen tok/s (empty) / 43.0 at 45k fill, prompt 1,317-1,776 tok/s, but only with forced num_gpu 66 at 48k ctx (default placement spills to 62/66 at 48k and drops to 24.8). Caveats: gen TPS falls with fill: Q2_K_L 58.4 empty -> 44.5 at 61k fill at 64k ctx, still fully resident, so 64k is reachable on Q2_K_L today with q8_0 KV; Q3_K_M/Q3_K_L stay slow (15-22) at 32k because they spill to CPU, Q3_K_M only recovers (44-47) at 8k ctx. Empty-ctx prompt TPS is meaningless (31-token prompt); use the filled figures. All numbers are throughput only, no quality ranking, and the KV q4_0 and fine-tune legs of the tuning run are not in yet; full report follows when the subagent finishes.

ACK overnight quality queue, no commits, no fleet config changes. Order: (1) GPU tuning legs finish (KV q4_0, fine-tune candidates; ~1-2 h). (2) v2 suite (14 tasks, 12_regex..25_undo, the one that separated low vs medium on OR) at medium thinking, 2 trials, on Q2_K_L@32k then Q3_K_S@32k then Q3_K_M at the largest ctx the tuning shows fully resident (16k with q4_0 KV if it fits; skipped with a note if only 8k). Est 3-4 h per quant at ~9k out tokens/run, ~10-11 h total. (3) v3 hard subset (32_wirefmt..36_minilang) same three quants, ~1.5 h each. (4) If time remains, third trial on v2 for the top two quants. Reference for quant loss: the same model unquantized, OR qwen3.8-27b fp8 ZDR at medium, already have v2-medium 44/55; I'll run the v3-hard reference at medium on OR in parallel since it does not touch the GPU. Grading is the same hidden tests + partial SCORE credit, so the ranking is pass rate and mean score per quant vs the fp8 reference, alongside the gen tok/s already measured. Lights-out: chained by one harness process with tree-kill timeouts, RAM/VRAM logged per model swap. Morning summary will lead with the quality-vs-speed ranking. Nothing needs a decision before morning unless Q3_K_M cannot be made resident above 8k, in which case I will just report it as not a candidate.

v4 ETA: the harder round in flight (tasks 32-36 + extra 31_stackvm trials) finishes in ~1-1.5 h, but it will NOT be a discriminating suite: 8/8 passes so far at LOW (32_wirefmt 3/3, 33_spanmap 3/3, 34_tmplfix 2/2), same as round 1 (46/48). A suite that actually separates quants needs another authoring round; realistic landing ~4-5 h from now (about 05:00). OPTIONS, owner's call: (A) tonight's workhorse = the discriminating subset we already have (12_regex, 15_diff, 17_interp, 21_query, 27_semver, 31_stackvm) at 5+ trials per quant for statistical power, ready now, no authoring risk; (B) author v4 now: Opus overseer writes 8-10 tasks aimed at 40-70% fp8 pass at medium with partial-credit SCORE grading, selftest validation, hidden tests, fp8 reference 3 trials on OR (~2-3 h), then swap into the GPU queue at the next model boundary; (C, recommended) both: start (A) on the GPU the moment tuning ends, author (B) in parallel on OR, swap v4 in when its reference is done, so the GPU never waits on authoring. What remains for v4 under (B): task generation (all of it; the current authors' 'harder' tasks still pass), selftest2 validation, hidden test.py per task, fp8 reference run; nothing blocks it except OR spend (~$ modest) and the fact that three authoring rounds have failed to find the edge, so v4 should be designed from the observed failure modes (regex engine semantics, diff/interp/query correctness under many hidden cases, semver/stackvm edge cases) rather than 'harder' in general. Swap-in is realistic: the queue is one harness invocation per (quant, suite), so v4 slots in at the next boundary without stopping anything. If I hear nothing I proceed with (C).

ACK option B. Revised queue: GPU: tuning legs to completion (~1-2 h) -> tuning follow-ups / extra tok/s sweeps (KV q4_0 at 64k on Q3_K_S forced-66, Q3_K_M ctx ladder 12k/16k/20k with q4_0 KV, prompt-fill curves) until the new round is ready -> quality runs on the new suite: Q2_K_L@32k, Q3_K_S@32k, Q3_K_M at its largest resident ctx, 2 trials each first (~3 h per quant at ~8 min/run), then a third trial pass; v2 subset NOT run. OR: v3 (32-36 + extra 31_stackvm) finishes as is (~1 h); the new failure-mode round is already underway (started before your reply, matches B exactly): Opus overseer + 3 Opus authors, 12 candidates from the observed failure modes (regex/glob semantics, decimal rounding, NULL aggregation, interp/undo state, diff/query correctness under randomized hidden cases), selftest-validated, hidden differential tests with SCORE partial credit, 3-trial fp8 medium reference on OR as the keep/reject filter (keep 1/3-2/3 or mean SCORE<0.9), target 8-10 keepers. Directory is named tasks-v4 in the bench tree only for ordering; I will call it 'the new round' in reports. Expected ready ~05:00; quality runs then take until roughly midday for two trials on three quants. No commits, no fleet config changes. Morning summary will lead with the quality-vs-speed ranking.

Plan file: C:\Users\slb\ollama-bench\results\overnight-plan-2026-09-03.md (v2). Audit outcome: GLM 17 findings, qwen3.8-27b 14; all material ones folded in, GPU and authoring never paused. Note: the 27B reviewer was the same model on OpenRouter, not the local Ollama copy, because the GPU was mid-tuning and one-model-at-a-time holds. Material findings and what changed: (1) HIGH, both: per-quant num_ctx and KV type would confound the ranking, and the harness --num-ctx flag does not reach task runs (only the TPS probe; the q27-* Modelfiles bake 32768, verified with ollama show, so qwen's '4-8k default' claim was wrong). Fix: one controlled config for all quants, 32k + q8_0 KV; Q3_K_M runs there even though it spills (slow, not invalid); any q4_0 'best config' run is a labelled extra after the controlled pass; env restored and asserted before the quality step. (2) HIGH, both: 2 trials on binary pass rate cannot rank quants. Fix: 3 trials mandatory and all-or-nothing across quants, mean SCORE primary with bootstrap CI, ranking stated only if CIs separate. (3) HIGH, qwen: PASS implies SCORE 1.0, so the keep filter's '3/3 with mean SCORE<0.9' branch was unreachable and the filter was 3 coin flips. Fix: score band, keep 0.25-0.85, keep 0-0.25 flagged as hard, reject 0 and >0.85; brief updated and the v4 overseer told. (4) MED: no watchdog existed for the leak-stop rule. Fix: a detached 10 s sampler (VRAM, Ollama RSS, free RAM, loaded-model count) is running now, results/gpu-watch.log, alert marker checked at task boundaries. (5) MED: fp8-vs-local delta conflates serving stacks; reported as an upper bound, quant-vs-quant on the same stack is the ranking. (6) MED: filler list is finite; now loops until v4 lands. (7) The 'morning report' cannot contain the ranking: Q3_K_M at 32k is slow, 3 trials x 3 quants lands afternoon or evening. Fix: 08:00 interim (tuning, 64k, authoring, trials so far), ranking sent when complete. Reviews archived at results/plan-audit/.

D1 Control plane: 1.3 kB pointer keeping imperatives in line vs keep ~2.5 kB with H3s -> pointer. D2 accept org/agents.md as a new 4 KiB undated page vs push those facts into CLAUDE.md -> accept. D3 Linux converge baselines: new dated file vs addendum on windows-play-profile -> new file. D4 orphan-clone consequence: drop (already in repo-merge-2026-08-26) vs keep in pending.md -> drop. D5 validator prescribed like the other gates vs add pre-commit (repo never had one) -> prescribed. D6 one dated FRACTAL file with the 08-16 outage as a section vs two -> one. D8 README ceiling 12,288 B (target ~11 kB) vs 10,240 -> 12,288. D9 one commit vs pure-addition commit then the cut -> one (but nothing is committed without your word). D11 accept two deletions with no surviving copy (2.1.257->258 hand-update record; Sync bullet wording history), git log keeps them -> accept. SUMMARY: README is actually 45.8 kB / 705 lines / nine H2 (Roles landed today); it becomes a pure index under a 12 KiB hard ceiling with H3s under Machines and Fleet capabilities and per-section budgets. New files: org/agents.md (4 KiB cap, only what CLAUDE.md and dated files lack), org/pending.md, three dated evidence files (windows-dns-leak, opus-subagents, converge-performance). Control plane becomes a pointer that keeps its imperatives in line (they exist nowhere else and /org delivers only the README). The org skill becomes index + routing table (the vrchat-avatars pattern) rather than per-section reads, because three of four harnesses have no argument channel. New scripts/validate-org-docs.py enforces the ceilings and CLAUDE.md==AGENTS.md, joining the gate block in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/README. Corrections to the brief: plan-usage bullet is 1.9 kB not 4.6; 129 commits not 45; there is no 'skill audit' in the repo (Verify_Agent_Skills is a Windows-only SHA check), so the ceiling needs a new gate. Strongest objections: GLM: agents.md would become the next 45 kB file -> capped at 4 KiB, single-home rule, shrunk to ~3.2 kB. qwen: move map had a 2.4 kB gap in the FRACTAL bullet so 'nothing deleted' was false -> full 705-line allocation ledger required before any cut.

v2 campaign done: low vs medium on OR qwen3.8-27b (Parasail pin verified) is NOT separable: low 41/54 (75.9%) vs medium 44/55 (80.0%), Fisher p=0.65, paired sign test p=1.0 over 14 tasks; verified by me (selftest2 tasks-v2 OK, v2-analyse.py reproduces the numbers). What differs is cost, not accuracy: at low the model flails on the hardest tasks (12_regex 26k vs 15k out tokens, 23_glob 50k vs 20k, 17_interp 33k vs 9k), so on this suite low is slower and dearer than medium, reversing the v1 finding. Failures are real model mistakes, mostly the same edge-case families v4 targets (15_diff imported banned difflib x5, 23_glob bracket/escape x4, 21_query null semantics, 24_fixed sign/ties, 12_regex nested quantifiers); timed-out runs counted as fails. GLM 5.3 Flash reference 1 trial: low 12-13/14, medium 10-11/14, so nothing is impossible by construction. Six graders/prompts were fixed and affected trials re-run (17_interp boolean 'application' wording was the big one). Spend ~1.9 upper bound, under the 0 cap. Artefacts: results/v2-low, v2-medium, v2-glm-*, v2-analyse.py, v2-campaign.log.

v3 campaign done (verified: selftest2 tasks-v3 OK, 17 tasks): fp8 at LOW passes 55/57; only separators are 34_tmplfix 2/3 (mean SCORE 0.88, floor 0.64), 27_semver 5/6, 31_stackvm 5/6; fp8 at MEDIUM on the hard five went 8/10 (32_wirefmt 1/2, 35_ledger 1/2). Headline finding, and it changes how v4 must be written: the model is not limited by spec difficulty, it writes its own tests and iterates until they pass, so anything a developer would think to test gets fixed. Its failures are (a) un-self-testable strictness it never thinks to check (leading zeros in prerelease ids, one opcode's underflow guard, [z-a], escape ordering, template whitespace control) and (b) violating explicit bans (difflib, time.time). Also the partial-credit graders were inverted on first run (empty sandbox scored 0.95); all 17 were rewritten to a fixed SCORE contract and re-measured, stale results discarded. Spend -12, under the 5 cap. pibench.py gained parse_score/SCORE support (backward compatible). Consequence for tonight: v4 smoke so far has 40_shquote, 41_csvdialect, 42_pathnorm all 3/3 (saturated, will be rejected under the score band); I have redirected the v4 overseer's next author round at strictness checks and enforced bans as separate SCORE items, with partial credit weighted so 'works on valid input' lands near 0.5-0.7, and NOT at tighter timeouts (that would rank quant speed, not quality). v4 readiness likely slips past 05:00; the GPU stays on the tuning filler loop meanwhile.

A second runaway model-written script (19 GB, +1 GB/min) was seen under a pibench run before exiting on its own, so pibench now has a memory guard that kills the tree past 8 GB per process / 20 GB total, tested. GPU is not idle: filler run started at 02:41, v3 hard five at medium, one trial each on Q2_K_L, Q3_K_S, IQ3_M, Q3_K_M (controlled config), interruptible at model boundaries when v4 lands. v4 smoke: 40-42 saturated at 3/3, authors re-targeting on strictness; a rewritten 54_sedlite scores a lax-but-valid solution at 0.63, in band. No commits, no fleet config changes. Full tuning tables in results/gpu-tune/summary.md.
